clue.text: Larry bothered about four in contention

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled name goes round the next piece
bothered suggests the letters of the name Larry are upset and jumbled

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone called Larry is fretting over four things in dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' makes RALRY, the anagram of the name, and 'about' says it surrounds the numeral; 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Contention between competitors is the same thing as competition or a contest for advantage.

clue.text: Where cheque that has not arrived had been mailed?

definitions.text: Where cheque that has not arrived had been mailed?

parts.words: Where cheque that has not arrived had been mailed?
parts.note: the stock excuse for a late payment is that it has already been sent, so the cheque is somewhere in the mail system

explanation.surface: A debtor's excuse about a payment that never turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque sent but not yet delivered is still travelling through the mail, the classic delaying excuse.

clue.text: Record depression

parts.note: the surface suggests a record low in mood or economy, but it means the spiral channel cut into a vinyl disc

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about the worst slump ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record carries a spiral channel cut into its surface, a literal hollow in the disc.

clue.text: Presumably it is not for heavy drinkers

definitions.text: Presumably it is not for heavy drinkers

parts.words: Presumably it is not for heavy drinkers
parts.note: heavy drinkers means people who drink a lot, but read literally it is the opposite of a beer described as not heavy

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain drink is meant for moderate imbibers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs a light ale is a pale bottled beer, while 'heavy' is a Scottish name for a darker bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale, low-strength bottled beer is named as the opposite of a heavy one.

clue.text: Wales, first person's ancestral home

explanation.surface: Wales described as the homeland of one's forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: Land of My Fathers is the English title of the Welsh national anthem, so it stands for Wales; 'first person' is the grammar term for I/me, giving MY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh anthem's English title is a byname for the country, and literally it describes the country where my forefathers lived.

clue.text: Go north of the border to terrain that's the world of crime

parts.note: gang is the Scots verb for go, and Scotland lies north of the English border
terrain is ground or land

explanation.surface: Moving across a frontier into a criminal underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangs of organised criminals and their territory make up the criminal underworld.

clue.text: Everybody individually starts trying first to instruct

indicators.note: first says that opening letter is placed before the other piece
starts here means the opening letter of the word trying

parts.note: each means every one taken separately

explanation.surface: Whoever wants to instruct should have everyone take turns at having a go.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to instruct or educate someone.

clue.text: Sideways after a time accompanying a novice

parts.note: later means after some time has passed
L is the learner plate worn by a novice driver

explanation.surface: Moving to one side some time later, alongside a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanying' is a link word joining the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral describes movement or position to the side, as in a sideways pass.

clue.text: Champion bridge player reaches target

parts.note: in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so W stands for West
the inner is the ring of a target just outside the bull

explanation.surface: A card player at the bridge table hits the bullseye and is crowned best.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the victor of a contest.

clue.text: Refusal in France by faction that's independent

parts.note: non is French for no
a party is a political faction or grouping

explanation.surface: A French no vote from one political group that stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent politician belongs to no political grouping.

clue.text: Cross had been removed from window-frame

indicators.note: removed here means shifted from their places, so the letters of cross and had are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crucifix has been taken down from a window frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been removed' makes the anagram of CROSS and HAD; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash cord is the rope in a sash window's frame that carries the counterweight.

clue.text: Learning about a hospital in Pakistan

definitions.note: the definition stands for a place in Pakistan, a city

indicators.note: about shows the word for learning goes round the following letters

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: Studying a hospital somewhere in Pakistan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'in Pakistan' stands for a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province and a major Pakistani city.

clue.text: Remove piece of paper from table

parts.note: to drop something is to remove or discard it
a leaf is a sheet of paper in a book

explanation.surface: Clearing a sheet of paper off a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-leaf is a kind of table with hinged flaps that fold down.

clue.text: Sole control is the name of the game

explanation.surface: Exclusive control is what it is all about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the name of the game' usually means the main point; here it literally names a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusive control of a market is the economic sense, and it is also the property-trading board game.

clue.text: Reinspect wreckage being far-seeing

indicators.note: wreckage suggests the letters of reinspect are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An investigator looks over a crash site again with foresight.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescient means having foreknowledge, able to see what will happen.

clue.text: Allow way out game

indicators.note: out stands for outside, so the word for way is placed around the word for allow

parts.note: a route is a way to go
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Permitting an exit from a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is an unusual container signal, read as 'outside'; it is not an anagram indicator here.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Total wreck, send it away

explanation.surface: Someone's ruined car is fit only to be got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: To write off for something is to send away by post for it; a car damaged beyond repair is also given this name by insurers.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurers use the term for a vehicle beyond economic repair, and the phrasal verb means to order something by sending a letter.

clue.text: Still be apologetic going round for money

indicators.note: going round says the word for be apologetic surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret or be sorry
even can mean still or yet, as in even better

explanation.surface: Still feeling sorry while going round asking for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, especially the money a business or government takes in.

clue.text: Dog dislodged bale, it can be put right

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: dislodged suggests the letters of bale are knocked out of place

explanation.surface: A dog knocked over a hay bale, but the damage can be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something curable can be remedied or healed.

clue.text: Roman statesman spent just over four weeks with you and me

parts.note: August has thirty-one days, a little more than four weeks
us means you and me together

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman politician passes about a month in our company.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus was the first Roman emperor, the great statesman who followed Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Middle part removed from rubbish put in outhouse

indicators.note: says the central letter of the word for rubbish is taken out

parts.note: garbage is rubbish or refuse

explanation.surface: Taking the core out of the rubbish before storing it in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The central letter of GARBAGE is B; 'put in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is an outbuilding for keeping a car.

clue.text: I, say, go after a positive declaration

indicators.note: go after says this piece follows the letter a
say tells us to use how the word for I sounds when spoken

parts.note: the letter I is a vowel

explanation.surface: Someone begins by stating something emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go after' puts the spoken form of VOWEL (from 'I') after A, so the whole thing sounds like 'a vowel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare openly, so an avowal is a frank, firm statement or admission.

clue.text: Partly unscrew his kitchen utensil

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Instructions to take apart a man's cooking gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisk is a kitchen tool for beating eggs or cream.

clue.text: Two men, first one heard vicious woman

indicators.note: says the first of the two names is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Harry is a man's name
Dan is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men argue, and the first is overheard by a nasty woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first one heard' applies the homophone only to the first name, spelt as the Welsh form Harri; the second name is written normally.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, bad-tempered old woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Excitedly expecting to open it out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of to open it are put out of order

explanation.surface: Eagerly waiting to pry something open.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on tiptoe is an idiom for being eager or keyed up with anticipation.

clue.text: Tame maggot

explanation.surface: A domesticated grub.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglers call a blowfly maggot used as bait a 'gentle', an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame means docile or mild, and the anglers' word for a bait grub is the same.

clue.text: Sounds like a ruin, the continental ship, how foolhardy

indicators.note: the clue opens by saying the first word is given as it is spoken

parts.note: a wreck is a ruin
le is French for the, masculine singular
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A rambling description of a wrecked foreign vessel and its rash crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless means rash and heedless of danger.
